sources.title: SOLAR-10.7B-Instruct-v 1.0 model card, pinned revision
sources.evidence: Identifies the exact SOLAR instruction-tuned checkpoint, its base-model relationship, DUS construction, SFT/DPO training, English text generation, and single-turn intended use. Explicitly assigns CC-BY-NC-4.0 to Instruct because noncommercial datasets were used, separately from the Apache-2.0 base model.

sources.title: SOLAR Instruct checkpoint configuration, pinned revision
sources.evidence: LlamaForCausalLM with 48 dense decoder layers, hidden width 4096, intermediate width 14336, 32 query heads, 8 KV heads, vocabulary 32000, untied word embeddings, no attention biases, float 16, max_position_embeddings 4096, and no RoPE scaling. No expert, quantization, multimodal, or auxiliary prediction module configuration.

sources.title: SOLAR Instruct five-shard tensor index, pinned revision
sources.evidence: Indexes all 435 tensors across five safetensors shards. The complete index was reconciled one-to-one with all five bounded headers and configured module names/shapes; total_size 21463048192 bytes equals the learned F 16 tensor payload.

sources.title: SOLAR Instruct original F 16 shard 1 bounded tensor header
sources.evidence: Read only the 8-byte safetensors length prefix and bounded JSON header via HTTP 206 byte ranges, not tensor payload. Across all five shards: 435 F 16 tensors, exactly 10731524096 learned elements, valid contiguous offsets and file lengths, and exact coverage of the pinned index and configured module shapes. No packed weights, scales, persistent buffers, adapters, or auxiliary heads appear.

sources.title: Transformers 4.35.0 Llama implementation matching checkpoint config
sources.evidence: Inspected configured modules: independent input embedding and output projection, RMSNorm learned scales, bias-free attention projections and three dense gated-MLP matrices per layer. RoPE frequencies/caches are nonpersistent buffers, not learned parameters. Names and shapes reconcile to all 435 indexed tensors.

sources.title: SOLAR Instruct text tokenizer and conversation template
sources.evidence: Defines LlamaTokenizer and a plain system/user/assistant text template. No declared tool-call/result roles or separate reasoning mode. The tokenizer model_max_length is a sentinel, so the configured 4096 positional limit is used.

sources.title: SOLAR 10.7B: Scaling Large Language Models with Simple yet Effective Depth Up-Scaling
sources.evidence: Technical report explains DUS as dense depth expansion to 48 layers, distinguishes it from MoE, and describes the instruction-tuned SOLAR model. Its 10.7B count is nominal. The Apache licensing link concerns the base checkpoint; it does not override the exact Instruct card. No separate active-parameter count or dedicated reasoning/tool-calling interface is specified.

sources.title: sDPO: Don’t Use Your Data All at Once
sources.evidence: Later first-party training research was checked for SOLAR 10.7B and the instruction-tuned model. It discusses dense Llama-based SOLAR, alignment methods and benchmark reasoning performance, but does not supply an independently defined active count or dedicated reasoning/tool-calling mode for this exact checkpoint.

sources.title: Upstage Solar 10.7B public availability announcement, December 14, 2023
sources.evidence: December 14 announcement says both pretrained and instruction-tuned versions are now available. Its blanket Apache-2.0 statement conflicts with the exact Instruct card and later developer response, so it is not used as the Instruct license. This is a later announcement, not evidence that December 14 was the earliest availability.

sources.title: Instruct license discussion and developer response, December 29–30, 2023
sources.evidence: Accessed through the Hugging Face discussion API. In response to the noncommercial instruction-training datasets, Upstage’s hunkim distinguishes the Apache-2.0 base model and hopes for instruction tuning with commercially viable data. This supports the current card’s separate noncommercial Instruct license.

sources.title: NVIDIA SOLAR 10.7B Instruct documentation: original model release date
sources.evidence: Explicitly labels the model developer Upstage and Model Release Date December 13, 2023, linking the exact SOLAR-10.7B-Instruct-v 1.0 card. This is a third-party statement of original model release, not an inferred NVIDIA listing date; it corroborates the creator announcement and contemporaneous public repository interaction.

sources.title: Watt Counts: original inference-energy benchmark, Section 5.2 and Table 11
sources.publisher: Mauricio Fadel Argerich, Jonathan Fürst and Marta Patiño-Martínez; Universidad Politécnica de Madrid and Zurich University of Applied Sciences
sources.evidence: Fresh original HTML and full PDF inspected, including a visual check of Table 11 on PDF page 17. The exact upstage/SOLAR-10.7B-Instruct-v1.0 row reports Total Params (B) 10.700 and Active Params (B) 10.700, with evaluation on eight GPUs. Section 5.2 defines the authors’ dense-model benchmark convention as active equal to total. Appendix C reports actual Solar measurements and explicitly recognizes its depth-upscaled architecture. This supports nominal active 10.7B under this independent research convention, not an Upstage disclosure or a measured token-specific tensor census.

sources.title: ERRORQUAKE: active-size plot and model-identification limitations
sources.evidence: Fresh full HTML reviewed. Figure 2 plots active size and includes solar-10.7b, but the source does not identify the exact Solar repository/checkpoint. Appendix D directs readers to Appendix N for active counts and architecture labels; Appendix N instead supplies leave-one-out correlations. The study also includes mistral-medium-3 within its open-weight dense roster without resolving that identity. Its untraced Solar plot label is not used to establish this exact checkpoint’s active count.

sources.title: Instruction-tuned Quantized Small Language Models: original Solar/Mixtral comparison
sources.publisher: Elijah Soba, Harika Abburi, Nirmala Pudota and colleagues, Deloitte; CEUR Workshop Proceedings
sources.evidence: Fresh full seven-page original proceedings paper reviewed. Sections 3.3/4 and the conclusion describe Solar 10.7B and Mixtral 8x7B as having fewer than 15B active parameters. That is only a bound, not an exact Solar active size; the paper also studies separately quantized and QDoRA-tuned derivatives. It is not the source of the adopted 10.7B active count.

name.note: Display punctuation normalized from the exact upstream repository name; retains Instruct and v 1.0 identity.

developer.note: Released by the original Upstage organization and documented by its authors.

family.note: Exact Instruct variant belongs to the SOLAR family; this is not a derivative community merge.

release_date.note: Earliest explicit launch found is the creator’s December 13 announcement as preserved by a mirror; NVIDIA independently labels December 13 as the original model release date, and public community interaction also exists that day. December 12 is an upload timestamp, not a verified public launch. Direct creator-post access remains unavailable, so the record is marked secondary rather than primary for release provenance; December 14 company PR is later.

open_weights.note: The original complete checkpoint is publicly downloadable. Open weights does not imply a commercial-use license.

license.note: Exact current Instruct card explicitly applies CC-BY-NC-4.0 because of noncommercial instruction-training data. Preserve it; Apache-2.0 applies to the base model, despite the older broad press-release statement.

parameters_b.note: Retain the original audit’s complete count of 10,731,524,096 learned parameters (10.731524096B), reconciled across all 435 F16 tensors and five bounded headers. Freshly reopened pinned config and index still specify 48 layers, width 4096, intermediate width 14336, 32000 vocabulary, untied embeddings and 21,463,048,192 F16 payload bytes. Recomputed configured count: 2×32000×4096+4096+48×[2×4096×(4096+1024)+3×4096×14336+2×4096]. Both embedding/output matrices are counted; nonpersistent RoPE buffers are excluded. The creator card and original report separately support nominal 10.7B. The previous header reconciliation is retained; no weight shards or headers were requested in this re-audit.

active_parameters_b.note: Nominal 10.7B under the Watt Counts authors’ published benchmark convention: Table 11 explicitly identifies upstage/SOLAR-10.7B-Instruct-v1.0 and lists 10.700B active; Section 5.2 defines its convention for dense models. The study reports this exact checkpoint’s inference measurements on eight GPUs and recognizes the DUS architecture. Attribute this to Fadel Argerich, Fürst and Patiño-Martínez, not Upstage. It is not a claim that precisely 10.7B individual learned parameters participate for every token; the exact total remains 10.731524096B. No active-count transfer from the structurally smaller Mistral 7B ancestor is used.

architecture.note: 48-layer dense decoder-only Llama transformer with grouped-query attention and dense SwiGLU-style MLPs. DUS changes depth; it does not add experts or sparse routing. Every configured projection and MLP is reconciled to the checkpoint.

context_window.note: Pinned max_position_embeddings is 4096 with no RoPE scaling. The tokenizer’s very large model_max_length is an unspecified-limit sentinel, not a supported context length.

modalities.note: Exact card, tokenizer and complete causal-language-model configuration establish text input and output; no other modality encoder or decoder is present.

reasoning.note: General reasoning benchmark performance and instruction training do not establish a dedicated reasoning mode. No exact-variant explicit positive or negative capability declaration was found in the card, template or original/later training reports; clear the unsupported false baseline.

tool_call.note: No exact-variant tool-calling contract or explicit lack-of-support statement was found. The plain role template has no tool definitions/call/result format, but omission alone does not prove false; clear the unsupported baseline assertion.

description.value: Instruction-tuned SOLAR text model built with depth up-scaling and optimized for single-turn conversation.
description.note: Matches the exact card. Replaces single-turn chat because the authors explicitly caution that the model is less suitable for multi-turn chat.

patch.description: Instruction-tuned SOLAR text model built with depth up-scaling and optimized for single-turn conversation.
patch.notes: Exact original F16 checkpoint contains 10,731,524,096 learned parameters across 435 tensors; 10.7B is the nominal name. Watt Counts Table 11 reports this exact checkpoint at 10.7B active under the authors’ nominal dense-model benchmark convention, not an Upstage per-token disclosure. CC-BY-NC-4.0 applies to Instruct; the base model uses Apache-2.0. December 13, 2023 is the explicit model-release date reported by NVIDIA and corroborated by the mirrored creator announcement; December 12 is only an upload timestamp, and direct access to the original announcement was unavailable. Dedicated reasoning/tool-calling support is unverified.

sources.label: Watt Counts exact-checkpoint nominal active-count convention

summary: Fresh parameter re-audit retains the complete 10.731524096B learned total and resolves nominal active size to 10.7B from the exact checkpoint row in the original Watt Counts benchmark, with its counting convention and independent authorship stated explicitly. Creator card/config/index and original SOLAR/sDPO reports were rechecked; ERRORQUAKE’s ambiguous plot and the CEUR less-than-15B bound are not used as exact-count evidence. All twelve other field assessments are preserved, including dense architecture, 4096 text context, CC-BY-NC-4.0, December 13 release with secondary provenance, single-turn intended use and unverified dedicated reasoning/tool-calling support.

parameter_reaudit.outcome: Retain precise 10.731524096B total; establish nominal active 10.7B from an original exact-checkpoint research benchmark.
parameter_reaudit.lineage_assessment: The exact creator card identifies an instruction fine-tune of SOLAR-10.7B-v1.0. The original technical report explicitly constructs the base by expanding 32 Mistral-initialized layers to 48 and then continuing pretraining; therefore an unchanged 7B active-count transfer would be invalid. The accepted active evidence directly names the Solar Instruct checkpoint and requires no ancestor transfer.
parameter_reaudit.search_findings: Fresh creator/card/index/config and original SOLAR/sDPO reports retain nominal 10.7B and do not separately disclose active counts. A fresh search led through a paper index to the original Watt Counts arXiv HTML/PDF. Table 11 supplies an explicit exact-ID active column and Section 5.2 states the authors’ convention; Appendix C contains Solar measurements. The adopted 10.7 is nominal, despite the table’s padded three-decimal formatting. ERRORQUAKE lacks exact checkpoint identification and its referenced numeric appendix; CEUR provides only a less-than-15B bound. Secondary model directories were not used as active-count evidence.
parameter_reaudit.source_quality_assessment: Watt Counts is an original inference study, with exact Hub IDs and measurements, rather than a model directory. Some unrelated rows misclassify MoE models (including Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat) as dense; this cautions against transferring its table wholesale. The Solar row’s dense classification, identity and nominal size independently agree with Upstage’s exact artifacts, and the study explicitly discusses Solar’s depth up-scaling. Thus its stated nominal active convention is usable for this row only, with attribution; it is not an independent active-tensor census.
parameter_reaudit.access_limitations: The web reader could not open the raw pinned Hugging Face README, but a direct original URL fetch returned HTTP 200. All three fresh pinned card/config/index fetches succeeded. No gated artifacts or weight shards were requested.
parameter_reaudit.remaining_uncertainty: No Upstage separately defined active-per-token count or exact token-dependent participation census was found. The catalog value is the explicitly attributed nominal research convention.
